abstract: The objective of the study in this paper is to find the possible effects of electromagnetic interference (EMI) on the performance of an information systems which is composed of radar systems, communication stations, and an information processing center. The topology of the information system under study is presented. The performance of the information system especially the digital communication system is evaluated. The possible EMI sources are mainly from neighboring radar systems. This analysis is to help achieve the optimal design of the information system under the EM environment.

articleTitle: Site attenuation characteristics of anechoic chamber using foamed ferrite as new absorbing material
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: The anechoic chamber built in the Kyushu Institute of Technology in 1998 can be configured as a semi-anechoic chamber as well as a fully anechoic one in the frequency range of from 30 MHz to 10 GHz, having a thickness of about 10 cm by using a foamed ferrite as the new absorbing material. The normalized site attenuation (NSA) of the fully anechoic chamber is within /spl plusmn/4 dB to the theoretical value in the frequency range from 30 MHz to 18 GHz, and the NSA of semi-anechoic chamber is also within /spl plusmn/4 dB to the NSA specified by CISPR in 30 MHz-1 GHz.

articleTitle: Anechoic chamber using foamed ferrite for immunity tests in the frequency range over 1 GHz
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: A new generation of electromagnetic absorber, which has pyramid shape and is 10 cm in height and has good absorbing characteristics in the range of high frequency range, was developed to satisfy the requirements of anechoic chambers. It was formed by a foaming process following sintering. When it was composed on a conventional ferrite tile, excellent absorbing characteristics over 20 dB were obtained in a wide range of frequency. At the same time, an anechoic chamber using foamed ferrite presented excellent uniformity of electromagnetic field strength.

articleTitle: The research of a new type aperture-coupled microstrip antenna
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: A new type dual-frequency dual-polarization aperture-coupled microstrip antenna is described in this paper. This antenna has broadband performance, that can get to 240 MHz when VSWR is less than 2.0 in 1.3 GHz and 200 MHz when VSWR is less than 1.5 in 700 MHz. The isolation between these two antennas is less than -45 dB, the structure of this antenna is compact, simple and easy to fabricate.

articleTitle: A study evaluation method for line noise filters using common mode output impedance of electrical equipment
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: Line noise filters are used to suppress conductive noise of electrical equipment and apparatus. Performance of these filters is evaluated by insertion loss. Such evaluation requires the output impedance for common mode noise from equipment. However, the impedance of the equipment under operation is not examined in general. This paper examines the output impedance of the equipment under operation. First, the impedance values are obtained by measurement. From evaluation results of the filter's (common mode capacitor) insertion loss, it is shown that impedance obtained in this paper is effective for verification of line noise filters. Next, an equivalent circuit of the equipment is studied. It is shown that impedance calculated from this equivalent circuit is also effective.

articleTitle: A study on suppression of induced voltage on printed wire by external electromagnetic field
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: One of the most effective ways to prevent malfunctions in electronic apparatus caused by external electromagnetic waves is to develop techniques that effectively suppress the voltage in printed wiring boards caused by these waves. In this paper, the differences in suppression effect that component insertion positions have was discussed when impedance component such as ferrite beads are used. The electromagnetic simulation was used to determine the distribution of voltage and current induced in the wiring when a printed wiring board was placed in an external electromagnetic field, and the relationship between impedance component insertion position and suppression effect was studied by simulation and experiment. Simulation results showed that the impedance component produced the greatest suppression effect at a position one quarter of a wavelength away from the end of a line at which the induced voltage is measured, and experiments confirmed the evidence. Also, suppression effect of resister and chip ferrite beads was compared and it was found that the effect of ferrite beads can be estimated from the impedance value.

articleTitle: An evaluation of bit errors due to the random fluctuation of atmosphere and ionosphere in satellite communication
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: For constructing satellite communication systems with high speed and large capacity, it becomes important to analyze quantitatively effects of the atmosphere and ionosphere. This paper deals with bit errors caused by arrival-angle fluctuation, sometimes called spot dancing. The analysis of bit errors is based on a multiple scattering theory of wave propagation in random media and the link model of the Communications and Broadcasting Engineering Test Satellite (COMETS) at the Ka band (20.7 GHz). At the Ka band the bit errors are affected by atmospheric fluctuations, but not by ionospheric fluctuations. The bit errors can not be neglected if the elevation angle becomes less than 10 [deg.] and a strong atmospheric fluctuation intensity is assumed.

articleTitle: Near- and far-fields test system of portable radios EMI to electronic devices
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: A new EMI (electromagnetic interference) test system to estimate the immunity of electronic devices is proposed. This system directly exposes the devices to the near- and far-fields generated by a dipole antenna and/or actual mobile phone. In addition, an in-vitro experimental system for pacemaker EMI investigation is introduced. This method uses the antenna input power and the distance between antenna and device-under-test as the test parameters instead of E-field strength. The transmitting signal properties of present mobile phones in Japan (800 MHz- and 1.5 GHz-PDC, 1.9 GHz-PHS, etc.,) are clarified to analyze EMI due to mobile radio wave exposure. A practical test procedure is also described. The summarized experimental results of EMI tests conducted on 228 pacemakers and 499 medical devices are shown to confirm the fact that the proposed system is indispensable for the EMI assessment of mobile phones.

articleTitle: Suppression of TV-ghosts caused by suspension bridge using a wave absorber
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: A vertically-polarized electromagnetic wave is strongly scattered by the hanger ropes of a large suspension bridge. Sometimes this causes a TV-ghost problem. This TV-ghost problem was theoretically calculated. Then, cylindrical wave absorbers constructed from a combination of dielectric and magnetic material were designed to suppress the scattering. This paper theoretically shows that using this absorber decreases the TV-ghost problem.

articleTitle: Calculation of surge attenuation in filters
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: Some standards set an attenuation of voltage pulses in uninterrupted power systems (UPS) and protection devices. These equipment have to be tested in an accredited laboratory for a compliance check. The proposed equivalent circuit gives the possibility to calculate attenuation beforehand. Results of computer simulation of surge propagation in LC-filters help to choose a filter for protection devices.

articleTitle: EMI problems for frequency hopping communication sets
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: To combat electromagnetic interference and to cope with jamming conditions of communication systems, in crowded radio frequency environments, the approach in radio system design is slowly directed towards frequency hopping radio sets. This paper includes features of frequency hopping sets and limitations in MIL-STD-462 towards EMC measurements/testing of such communication systems/sets. Possible methods that may be adopted for such measurements are discussed in this paper.

articleTitle: Measurements of potential distributions near flat boards
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: The authors have developed two types of 2-dimensional measurement systems that measure the potential distribution near electrified flat boards. One system is based on one accurate potential sensor with a mechanical scanning structure; the other system is based on an array of low cost FET probes. These systems show charge distribution on the board. The characteristics of these systems are certified using simply formed printed circuit boards (PCB). Examples of the entirely or partially charged PCB are also shown.

articleTitle: Logic and evaluation of assuring functional safety from electromagnetic noise
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: The logic of assuring functional safety from electromagnetic noise is discussed. A configuration example is given of a sensor system hierarchically provided with electromagnetic noise-tolerant capability and electromagnetic noise-resistant capability. Today's international safety standards specify the evaluation of functional safety from the component failure of the system on the basis of the safety assurance process to be performed by the system. Functional safety from electromagnetic noise is evaluated only according to behavior test results. The meaning of the electromagnetic noise requirements specified in the safety standards is clarified in relation to the logic of evaluating functional safety from faults. To achieve high functional safety from electromagnetic noise, it is logically demonstrated that the processing system must have a structure resistant (or fail-safe) with respect to electromagnetic noise. Structures for assuring functional safety from electromagnetic noise in the sensor systems developed by the authors are presented.

articleTitle: Development of wide band ferrite fin electromagnetic wave absorber for glass curtain wall
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: A ferrite fin electromagnetic wave absorber is developed for a glass curtain wall. The ferrite fin absorber has been studied as a component structure of the ferrite grid absorber. Structure of the absorber is designed by calculation with transmission line method for oblique incidence. The characteristics are measured using mock-ups for the glass curtain wall with the time domain method. The developed absorber suppresses reflection below -17 dB in the frequency range between 80-800 MHz for incident angle, of 60/spl deg/. The absorber can be applied to the TV ghost problem in both of VHF and UHF bands.

articleTitle: Radiation from and current distribution on plane conductor
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: Plane conductors with a dipole antenna configuration are excited by disturbance sources. Far-field radiation, magnetic near field and current flow on the plane, and input impedance are analyzed numerically and experimentally. For the open-end structure, the current flows along the edge of the plane. The current path is equivalent to half of the wavelength, at the frequency corresponding to which the input impedance has minimum.

articleTitle: Limits, test methods and ISNs for emission and immunity on unshielded telecommunication ports
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: The new editions of CISPR 22/EN 55022 as well as CISPR 24/EN 55024 require testing of emission and immunity on telecommunication ports of information technology equipment (ITE) and telecommunication equipment. Different versions of impedance stabilization networks (ISNs) are required for the different conformance alternatives and cable categories. Since there is a great variety of systems with different pin connections of the RJ45 connector, a solution with a basic universal network using a universal interface and a series of adapters has been chosen. A high-performance balun is used for verification and calibration. Imperfections of the CISPR 22 standard are discussed together with suggestions for improved testing.

articleTitle: The amplitude selection technique of EMC prediction in communication system
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: In this paper, the amplitude selection technique is presented to predict and analyze the EMC of huge communication systems. Using this method, we can calculate the interference power at the input terminal of the receiver that is being interfered, and compare it with the threshold of sensitivity of the receiver to infer whether there is any interference.

articleTitle: RF-exposure system for the uniform exposure of a large number of biological samples
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: This paper gives an introduction to a completely shielded RF-exposure system designed on the basis of a radial waveguide that enables a well defined highly uniform exposure of a large number of biological samples. For easy handling of the biological samples, special openings allow the insertion and removal of the samples without any actuation of closures and without any decrease of the shielding effectiveness.

articleTitle: Transient-field characterization of reverse recovery behavior of diode with interconnection
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: A novel time domain analytical method based on the TLM for predicting transient fields of loop circuits during the reverse recovery period of a diode is presented. It enables the exact calculation of both the far and near field distributions for the transient process, which is necessary to verify the correct operation of the control unit in the power electronics converters. Retardation has to be taken into account in the calculation to ensure exact results. The computed results show good agreement with the measured ones.

articleTitle: Undergraduate EMC education at Xidian University
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: This paper describes the prerequisite courses and contents of a course in EMC given in the Department of Microwave Telecommunication Engineering at Xidian University, China. The resource extension technique taken during teaching the EMC course is presented in detail, meanwhile, the aim and effect of the course are outlined in this paper.

articleTitle: Calculation of normal-mode voltage on the balanced line converted from the injected common-mode voltage
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: The noise mode conversion on the balanced line from the common-mode to the normal-mode was investigated. Two simple parallel traces with the injected common-mode voltage were considered for the mode conversion. The normal-mode voltage converted was calculated from the eight terminals circuit theory. The effect of the mutual coupling between traces on the mode conversion was also examined. As a result, it was found that the tight magnetic coupling between the traces gave less mode conversion.

articleTitle: Time domain analysis of nonsinusoidal electromagnetic waves in stratified conducting shields
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: We present a new approach to study electromagnetic wave transients in multiple layer shields in the time domain. New analytical solutions of Maxwell's equations modeling the wave propagation for arbitrary waveform functions in conductive media are applied. This provides new insights into physics of shielding by distinguishing between main wave parts and diffusive wave parts. Without loss of accuracy the method allows semi-numerical results even for Dirac-shaped pulses within a coarse grid. We derive impulse responses and demonstrate transient field computation via convolution.

articleTitle: A new dual-coaxial-TEM cell
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: Previously, different configurations of TEM cells, chambers and transmission-line holders were used to determine the intrinsic shielding effectiveness (SE) of materials e.g. conductive plastics. In this contribution, a new dual-coaxial-TEM Cell is presented which allows to measure the SE of materials, determine the influence of apertures and test analytical and numerical computation methods. The mechanical and electrical structure is described and the calculation of the electromagnetic coupling is verified by the results of measurements. In addition to the worst-case examination of structures (the electric field is perpendicular to the surface of the test-sample), the dual-coaxial-TEM Cell provides a wide frequency range and high dynamic.

articleTitle: New ISNs for emission and immunity testing on unshielded telecommunication ports
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: The new editions of CISPR 22/EN 55022 as well as CISPR 24/EN 55024 require testing of emission and immunity on telecommunication ports of information technology equipment (ITE) and telecommunication equipment. Signal transmission on unshielded telecommunication lines need transmission bandwidths up to 100 MHz for systems like "ISDN", "ATM" (asynchronous transfer modus), "ADSL", "VDSL", "FDDI" (fibre distributed data interface-with wired extensions), "token ring", "10BaseT" and "100BaseT". The paper discusses test procedures and requirements for ISNs.

articleTitle: A method for finding the direction of arrival of a single short pulse by the waveform reconstruction
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: A method for finding the direction of arrival (DOA) of a single short pulse is proposed. The method is based on a waveform reconstruction technique using complex antenna factors (CAF). Since the frequency characteristics of CAF has angle dependency, the DOA of an electromagnetic pulse can be determined by the waveforms reconstructed with CAF. The result of an experiment shows the possibility to apply the two-dimensional DOA finding.

articleTitle: Micro and millimeter wave absorber using M-type hexagonal ferrite
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: In this paper the authors describe how micro and millimeter wave absorbers using the ferrimagnetic resonance of M-type hexagonal ferrite have been developed for EMC research applications.
