articleTitle: Experimental investigation of controlling coverage of wireless LAN by using partitions with absorbing board
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: For a wireless communication system to work effectively without electromagnetic interference, the electromagnetic environment needs to be controlled. We experimentally investigated methods for controlling the electrical field strength and the delay spread so as to achieve communications without electromagnetic interference in selected regions for a 2.4-GHz-ISM-band wireless LAN system. Several indoor environments in which partitions with electromagnetic absorbing board were placed around desks were used. The transmission loss and delay spread were investigated experimentally, and the BER and throughput characteristics were measured. We found that the coverage of a wireless LAN could be controlled by using partitions with absorbing boards. We identified several requirements for controlling the coverage that should be useful in designing indoor wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: An experimental study on correlation between electromagnetic noise and trace of discharge in Cu-C electrodes-case of C (anode)-Cu (cathode)
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: The authors observed the correlation between electromagnetic noise and trace of discharge on surface in opening carbon(C)-copper(Cu) electrodes. In the case of C (anode)-Cu (cathode), continuous burst noise is generated over the period of arc discharge. When the discontinuous fluctuation of arc voltage occurs, the level of burst noise becomes high in that period. Arc discharge is classified into four periods based on features of the arc voltage and the burst noise waveforms. There are circular traces of discharge (area /spl alpha/) and a shiny melted area (area /spl beta/) on the electrode surface. When the period of high noise level becomes longer, area /spl alpha/ has wide distribution on the surface. When the period of low noise level in the middle of the arc becomes longer, area /spl beta/ distributes widely. The period of low noise level in the start of the arc has small correlation with the area /spl alpha/, /spl beta/. From these results, it is considered that arc discharge of three different types are mixed in one opening period of electrodes.

articleTitle: Experimental investigation of noise immunity diagnosis for printed circuit boards by bulk current injection test
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: A simple method for diagnosing noise immunity of printed circuit boards (PCBs) by the bulk current injection (BCI) test was proposed, which can contribute to the PCB trace designs for common-mode noise. A grading index, which is defined as the ratio of the stray capacitances with and without critical IC of malfunction, was introduced to distinguish PCBs susceptible to the common-mode noise. This proposed method was validated experimentally using four PCBs with the same circuit but different trace designs. It was observed that the noise immunity of PCBs had a good correlation with the values of these grading indices.

articleTitle: Experimental analysis of the human perception threshold of an ELF electric field
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: For the study of biological effects of ELF electric fields, a fundamental study has been conducted on a human perception threshold of electric field. The perception threshold was measured with human subjects and the results were analyzed. It was made clear that the field perception was based on the movement of the hair and not on other sensations. The variance in the perception threshold and its cause were investigated. The perception threshold decreased by almost 30% as the relative humidity increased from 50% to 90%. The perception threshold was also dependent on the physical condition (length and density) of the hair and psychological condition of the subject. The dependence on them was much smaller than that on the relative humidity. The cause of the gender difference of the threshold is ascribed to the difference in the physical condition of the hair. Through this study, some factors to be taken into account for the safety standard were made clear.

articleTitle: Reduction of electromagnetic radiation from power and ground layers using capacitors
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: Reduction of electromagnetic radiation using capacitors has been studied for power and ground layers in multilayer printed circuit boards. Capacitors placed near the board edges decreased the electromagnetic radiation from the power and the ground layer when they were arranged with an appropriate spacing. However, they activated another radiation noise. It was found that capacitors near ICs were effective to reduce the other noise. By placing an appropriate capacitance for the edge capacitors and for the near-IC capacitors, the electromagnetic radiation from the power and the ground layer was reduced drastically without exciting the other noise.

articleTitle: Study on the influence of ground on crosstalk reduction characteristics of twisted-pair-wire. The case of capacitive coupling
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: In this study, the influence of the location of a ground plane on the induced noise (crosstalk) on a twisted-pair-wire (TPW) by parallel lines is experimentally and theoretically discussed by paying attention to capacitive coupling between the TPW and the parallel lines. The capacity is obtained by applying the finite element method (FEM) to the calculation of electric field intensity. It is confirmed that calculated results are in good agreement with experimental results within 1 dB. It is concluded that the closer the TPW is to ground plane, the smaller the induced noise on the TPW becomes.

articleTitle: Simultaneous measurements of disturbance APD, CRD and PDD
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: A method is presented that can measure characteristic statistical parameters of disturbance, namely amplitude probability distribution (APD), crossing rate distribution (CRD) and pulse duration distribution (PDD). For APD and CRD, a circuit is realized that simultaneously measures these two parameters with an amplitude resolution equivalent to the number of quantized levels. For PDD, a new circuit is proposed that can execute real-time measurement of pulse duration histograms with a wide range. A simple modification of the circuit may simultaneously measure APD, CRD as well as PDD.

articleTitle: EMC problems of GSM 1800 cellular networks and radio relay systems of the fixed service in Russia
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: The paper deals with EMC problems of GSM 1800 cellular networks and radio relay systems in the 2 GHz band in Russia. The EMC analysis of GSM 1800 cellular networks and radio relay systems is developed on the basis of empirical-statistical model of radio waves propagation in urban areas. Putting into consideration the power and spatial parameters the required separation distances and frequency offsets between radio electronic devices of the mentioned systems are defined.

articleTitle: Measurement of power absorption by COST 244 human head model by using pattern integration method
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: The power absorption by the canonical human models proposed by the COST 244, i.e., homogeneous cubical and spherical models, located in the vicinity of antennas is measured by using the pattern integration method. A dipole antenna and a monopole antenna mounted on a conducting box are used at frequency of 1.5 GHz. The finite difference time domain (FDTD) analysis is also performed and the numerical results are compared with the experimental data. It is shown that the calculation agrees well with the measurement, which demonstrates the accuracy of the experimental setup.

articleTitle: Statistical analysis of radio frequency noise spectrum in Korea
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: Measurements of the RF (radio frequency) noise spectrum from 30 MHz to 18 GHz have been conducted in 1994, 1995, 1996, and 1997 at 21 urban areas in South Korea. Statistical analysis of the data measured seasonally, day and night, at each different point has been performed, and the results of the computer analysis on APD (amplitude probability distribution), NAD (noise amplitude distribution), and ACR (average crossing rate), using GUI (graphical user interface) program show that the radio noise environments vary little between spring, summer, and winter. On the contrary, the noise level increases a little in fall, and the noise level at night time is a little higher than that of the day time.

articleTitle: Novel decoupling circuit comprising magnetic materials and built-in choking coils
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: This paper describes a novel decoupling circuit comprising magnetic materials and built-in choking coils which makes it possible to significantly suppress noise and improve noise immunity in a digital printed circuit board (PCB).

articleTitle: An experimental study on the dependence of local SARs on a human ear during exposure to MW from a cellular telephone
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: Dependence of specific absorption rates (SARs) on the shapes of a human ear during exposure to microwave from a cellular telephone was experimentally evaluated. The local SARs were measured using an electric-field probe in a head phantom of a plastic cubical shell filled with brain-tissue-simulating liquid. It was shown that the shape of the ear strongly affected the SAR distribution in the human head. It was also shown that the measured SAR distributions agreed well with those obtained by the numerical simulation.

articleTitle: Estimation of non-Gaussian probability density of signals and interferences
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: The paper gives the resulting probability density of a set of signal (interference) parameters to describe a mixture of private probability densities. For definition of unknown parameters of private probability densities the method of maximal likelihood is used. The paper resolves the maximal likelihood equations for the practically important case when the private probability densities of moments of signal arrivals are subject to Gaussian law.

articleTitle: Radiation performance and evaluation of human exposure from mobile handsets using near-field measurements
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: The necessity of near-field evaluation in wireless product development will strongly grow in the coming years, since far-field evaluations provide insufficient information for analyzing and optimizing the performance of transmitters operating in complex environments. The objective of this paper is to review the latest progress in near-field measurement technology and to discuss future needs.

articleTitle: Modeling and analysis on pass-through current decoupling method for multi-layer printed circuit board
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: It is well known that pass-through current, caused by the output buffer circuit of an IC during its transient state, can be a dominant source of the radiated field from the printed circuit board (PCB). In this paper, a modeling method is proposed to analyze this radiated field with a full-wave electromagnetic simulator using the method of moments (MOM). An analysis on the decoupling method, specifically for the case in which the IC is placed on a multi-layer PCB with segmented power and ground plane structure, has been carried out and found that there is close relationship between the PCB layer structure and the adequate location of decoupling capacitors. Our simulated results showed that there is a case that a general rule "decoupling should be placed close to VCC pin" is not adequate. Measurements have also been done with experimental model and the results are presented.

articleTitle: Efficient analysis of coupled multiconductor transmission lines
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: Multiconductor transmission line equations are decoupled using Newton-Raphson iteration. Ambiguity arising from multiple eigenvalues is eliminated. Free and fixed parameters of the decoupling operators are clearly identified. By introducing new length variables, the complete coupled line system can be described by two simple partial differential equations. The method is fast and numerically stable.

articleTitle: Common mode current prediction from normal mode voltage of printed circuit board with limited width ground pattern
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: Radiated emission due to common mode current is usually dominant in total emission. The common mode current is generated when the ground width of the microstrip structure is narrow. A procedure is proposed to predict common mode current from normal mode voltage at a point where cross-sectional structure is varying. As a result, the predicted spectrum and distribution of common mode current agree well with measured data.

articleTitle: Three directional Helmholtz coils for a low frequency-magnetic-field immunity test
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: A magnetic field inside a space surrounding three sets of Helmholtz coils is studied to propose a new radiated immunity test method. The proposed immunity test set arranges the Helmholtz coils three dimensionally and is able to generate the magnetic field of arbitrary direction. Therefore the immunity characteristics of equipment under test for many directions can be measured by using this system. The uniformity of the field inside the space is estimated by numerical analysis, and then the effect for a radiated immunity test is characterized.

articleTitle: The use of scanning receivers in EMI compliance measurements
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: Spectrum analyzers and EMI receivers are both used to make radiated and conducted EMI measurements. In this paper, the hardware architectures of scanning and conventional receivers are compared in consideration of essential EMI receiver specifications and the still controversial fundamental practical considerations such as stepped versus swept frequency measurement, receiver frequency and display resolution, RF overload detection and narrowband and broadband signal discrimination.

articleTitle: Calculation of the field distribution around the body exposed to the emissions from cellular phones
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: Calculation of electric field strength distributions inside and outside the body, which is exposed to the emissions from the cellular phones, is made under several different conditions, by using the FDTD method with an imaginary microwave-absorbed material constructed the absorption boundary of the region under consideration. The cellular phone is modeled as a monopole antenna with a metal plate on its end and the height of it is /spl lambda//4. The electromagnetic numerical model of body in established on the basis of anatomy, in which, the different tissues are identified by different colors. The computational results show the different circumstances and the different position of the cellular phone will greatly affect the field distributions in the body.

articleTitle: FDTD analysis of power absorbed by anisotropic ferrite plate located in the vicinity of a microstrip line
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: The FD-FDTD (frequency dependent finite difference time domain) method using the recursive convolution is applied to a numerical analysis of power absorption by a ferrite plate. Since the ferrite is a gyro-magnetic material and has a permeability tensor, three components of the magnetic field are required for the numerical calculation at every node point of Yee cells. In order to avoid the difficulty, the interpolation technique is employed. Numerical results of the absorbed power by the ferrite plate near a microstrip line are shown and the suppression of undesired emission by the ferrite plate is observed especially in the resonance frequency range of the ferrite material.

articleTitle: A FDTD method for fast simulation of decoupling capacitors on multilayer multichip modules
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: We present a new method for the simulation of the power supply system on multilayer substrates of multichip modules (MCM). In particular we investigate the efficiency of extended high capacitance layers used as decoupling capacitors. The proposed method works with a lumped element FDTD technique which facilitates electromagnetic simulation of the substrate simultaneous with simulation of the mounted electronic circuit. The stratified configuration of multilayer structures allows division of the 3D problem into separate 2D problems. This yields an efficient algorithm. The algorithm has been implemented in C++ and tested with different examples. Furthermore we present reference data derived by analytical investigation of a circular plate capacitor. This data is used to evaluate the simulation results.

articleTitle: Deterioration in shield characteristics by signal lines and power lines passing through shield material
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: The authors are developing the technology for designing shields of electronic equipment. As a factor which deteriorates shield characteristics, we pay attention to signal lines and power lines passing through a shield material. In this paper, we describe the effects of these lines on shield characteristics.

articleTitle: Investigation of the error introduced by the thin wall approximation in shielding problems
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: If thin walls have to be discretized in the numerical treatment of shielding problems, the computation tends to be become cumbersome since the fine discretization needed in the thin shielding walls will enforce an overall mesh with a great number of nodes. To overcome this difficulty, a jump condition, approximately valid at thin shielding walls, is introduced. The error induced by this approximation is studied for a configuration for which the analytical solution is also known.

articleTitle: Experience of measuring normalized site attenuation at CMS
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: An open test site located at the Telecommunication Lab in Taiwan is characterized by measuring normalized site attenuation (NSA) to determine the suitability of this open test site for antenna measurement. The measured NSA data are compared to the theoretical values. The results show a maximum deviation of less than 3 dB over the frequency range of 30 to 1000 MHz.

articleTitle: The investigation of a millimeterwave microstrip antenna
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: A circular-aperture microstrip patch array antenna is described in the paper. The design methods and measurement results are also given. The gain of the antenna is 28 dB, the side lobe level is less than -15 dB, the beam width is 5, the bandwidth can reach 1.5/spl sim/2.0 GHz when VSWR is less then 2.0.

articleTitle: On the radiation from nonequi-length paired cable
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: The radiation from the nonequi-length paired cable was investigated theoretically and experimentally. The research reveals that the radiation spectrum has peaks, which locate at the resonance frequencies where not excess short line but total longer line length corresponds to n /spl lambda//2, even in case of matching termination. It is due to the common mode radiation.

articleTitle: Improved sensitivity in grounding search system using TV signal for phase reference
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: Grounding search systems need improved sensitivity to search more effectively for grounding routes. The proposed method changes the phase reference signal source from the search signal to a TV signal. A minimum signal level of 17 dBuV at the antenna terminal is needed to obtain the phase reference. Experimentation using the new system demonstrated an improvement of 40 dB in the minimum detectable level and the phase measurement deviation improved from /spl plusmn/18 degrees to /spl plusmn/8 degrees.

articleTitle: Very fast time domain measurement of voltage rising part due to micro gap discharge in air
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: Voltage rise and fall characteristics due to starting of very short gap discharge were investigated in time domain. The gap space was set very short for voltage below 1500 V as phenomena of CDM ESD and electrical contact of switch devices. The measurement system consists of a distributed constant line system with a coaxial type electrode, because the voltage transients were very rapid. The coaxial electrode has matched impedance for a characteristic impedance of semi-rigid cables of the distributed constant line system. An atmosphere around the coaxial electrode is normal air. This experimental system enables measurement of the high speed and high voltage transients of about 100 ps. As a consequence of the experiment, a relationship between source voltage and voltage rise and fall time were confirmed due to changed source polarity.

articleTitle: New approach for EMC design
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: This paper introduces newly developed absorbing material and grounding components of a PC board for EMC suppression design and their testing method.

articleTitle: Measurement of complex permittivity and permeability at millimeter wavelength using a free space method
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: Measuring permittivity and permeability of materials with the free space method is effective at higher frequencies because precisely shaped samples are less necessary. However, in the millimeter-wave range, accurate measurement is difficult because of the increase of errors in phase measurement. In this paper, the authors propose a method for phase error correction, which has been tested in actual measurements to confirm the effectiveness, and applied to a design for some millimeter wave absorbers.

articleTitle: Determination of a relevant criterion to characterize differential conducted perturbations generated by low frequency converters
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: This paper demonstrates that the slope is not an appropriate parameter to characterize a waveform regarding conducted electromagnetic perturbations. On the other hand, a relevant criterion is made conspicuous: it defines the maximum slope deviation between two segments forming a signal. This criterion is validated by a waveform with a maximum slope of 400 mA//spl mu/s.

articleTitle: Recent topics in activities of IEC and JIS in relation with EMC
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: The activities of the Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) in the field of EMC standardization at the international and national levels are reviewed. The situation of the regulations in Japan and the JIS related to EMC is also reported. The problems to be solved in the future are discussed.

articleTitle: Space-divided FDTD method [for electromagnetic problems]
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: A new numerical computation scheme that is used in the FDTD method is presented in this paper. This scheme divides the large calculation space that FDTD method needs into some sections and re-uses the computer's limited memory to load every section one by one and iterate in every section one by one. Using this method, a large scale electromagnetic problem can be handled. This method is used in some examples, the calculation data shows that this method is feasible and the results are correct compared with that obtained by normal FDTD method. This method can be used in the analysis and prediction of EMC/EMI problems.

articleTitle: Calculation of service area for mobile communication system using optical rays
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: Communication systems using optical rays are expected to be used in environments containing sensitive electronic equipment. This paper studies a method of calculating the service area for an optical mobile communication system. The service area is defined by the communication angle, which is calculated using ray-tracing theory considering reflections from materials in the room. The calculated results are compared with experimentally measured ones, and the difference is less than 12%.

articleTitle: Demonstration of radio noise measurement
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: This paper shows radio noise measurement in VHF band. Newly developed APD measuring equipment were used for this measurement together with a spectrum analyzer. Some results are given.

articleTitle: Evaluation of impedance-matching and coupling by using radiowave holograph method. I
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: A new method for evaluating microwave modules is proposed. The technique yields visualization of impedance mismatching points and electromagnetic coupling by using a radiowave holography method based on the near-field interference pattern measurement. Some results of the experiment are presented to demonstrate the validity of the proposed method.

articleTitle: The anomaly crosstalk of MF broadcast signals into the VLF receivers similar to the Luxembourg effects as one of the seismogenic phenomena
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: In December 19, 1997, at 22:09 (JST), an earthquake (M=4.6, D=10 km) attacked the north of Japan's Fikui prefecture. Prior of this main shock, a VLF sensor received a cross-talk signal from the MF broadcasting stations of Kanazawa. The authors present a theoretical analysis to explain this by using a type of the Luxembourg effects.

articleTitle: Calculation of the IEMP induced surface current on a thin cylinder
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: The inner electromagnetic pulse (IEMP) environment in a metallic hybrid cylindrical cavity is analyzed. To investigate the IEMP induced current in the cables within the cavity, the current on the surface of a thin cylinder is calculated. The calculation method and the results are presented.

articleTitle: Electromagnetically induced current in DC control lines generated from ferro-electric packed bed plasma reactors
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: A ferro-electric packed bed type plasma reactor is widely used in industrial ozonizer and toxic gas treatments. In this work, an electromagnetically induced current in nearby DC control lines generated from the intensive barrier discharge is experimentally and theoretically investigated.

articleTitle: Characteristics of noise on printed circuit board traces induced by noise transmitted on external cables
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: This study is for improving the noise immunity of electronic circuits on printed circuit boards (PCBs). The noise on the PCB traces is induced by external cables which are different from the PCB traces in length. This paper experimentally and analytically clarifies that large amounts of noise can be transferred from a noisy wire to a victim wire, even when the wires are of different length and loose coupling at a short-section. The reason why large amounts of noise are transferred is revealed that the base resonant frequency f/sub 0/ of the shorter wire's own can be the same as the multiple resonant frequency N/spl middot/f/sub 0/ (N=2,3,...) of the other wire's own. Further, according to the location and kinds of load such as ICs connected with the PCB trace, which is considered as a victim wire, the resonant frequency dominating the noise frequency is changed.

articleTitle: Analysis of electromagnetic wave scattering from building walls with periodic and random surface
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: In this paper, the authors numerically analyze the scattering of electromagnetic waves from building walls by using the FVTD method. They consider three different types of rough surfaces such as periodic, random, and composite structures. They calculate the bistatic normalized radar cross section (NRCS) for horizontal and vertical polarization, and take account of the conventional optical reflection which corresponds to the n-th Bragg reflection for periodic structures. In addition, they investigate what conditions are needed in order to be able to ignore the higher order Bragg reflection for the periodic structures.

articleTitle: Analysis of induced current density in spherical conductive model exposed simultaneously to extremely low frequency electric and magnetic fields
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: In this paper, the effects of electric and magnetic field components on the total induced current density in a homogeneous spherical conductive model exposed to 60 Hz electric and magnetic fields (electric field 1 kV/m, magnetic field 1 /spl mu/T) are investigated through computer analysis. The distribution profiles of the induced current density in the model exposed to extremely low frequency electric and magnetic fields in parallel with each other are almost dominated by the electric field. But the ones in the case of mutually orthogonal electric and magnetic fields are different; in other words, the total induced current densities are affected by the magnitudes and the phases of the fields.

articleTitle: A comment on some epidemiologic papers related to cancer and magnetic fields of power lines
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: Many epidemiologic papers on the relation between cancer and magnetic fields of power lines have been published. This paper presents a new interpretation of them. Some public panels that reviewed these papers stated that there is no conclusive evidence to show that magnetic fields cause cancer. Others stated that magnetic fields are carcinogenic. The difference between the conclusions of the panels is from discrepancies in interpreting the same papers. The author examined the reasoning of some epidemiologic papers from their premise to the conclusion and found that in a Swedish paper (Karolinska Inst.) there was a logical contradiction and in a Nordic pooled paper pooling data of a Danish, a Finnish and the Swedish studies there was a logical fallacy. Therefore, the author could not accept that their hypothesis "there is an association between power-line magnetic fields and childhood leukemia" was verified.

articleTitle: Analysis of voltage dips propagation in MV distribution networks by using ATP-EMTP code
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: In this paper, voltage dips simulation in electric power MV distribution networks by using an improved ATP circuit-breaker model are reported. An equivalent circuit of a MV distribution system is employed. The circuit-breaker is simulated by using a tool written in MODELS language and by arranging a time-variable differential arc-conductance based on the combination of Mayr's and Cassie's equations. The simulations carried out have shown how the amplitude of the voltage dips depends on the type and location of the fault and their duration is strictly related to the circuit-breaker parameters.

articleTitle: RF measurement method over 1 GHz
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: This report contains RFI testing results over 1 GHz using 0.5 m/spl times/0.5 m independent windows and compares the results with the results obtained by traditional method. The method is used to test a video camera as an example.

articleTitle: A transfer impedance measurement bench for high immunity [cables]
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: A measurement bench has been developed to determine the transfer impedance (Zt) of high immunity cables. The authors built a bench with a quadriaxial structure. To reach the high dynamic measurement range of their bench, they had to inject a 50 W signal; the signal analyzer was a spectrum analyzer inside a Faraday cage. To validate their test bench, they measured well-known commercial cables and compared results. Measurements they made were coherent with standard values. They achieved a sensitivity of 0.3 /spl mu//spl Omega//m up to 100 MHz.

articleTitle: Effect of membrane on current distribution in biological sphere tissue with a membrane placed in uniform and eddy current fields
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: Some experimental reports suggest the significant role of tissue membrane on the ELF magnetically induced current distribution, which is rarely implemented in a numerical procedure of induced current estimation. The paper presents an analytical examination of those results by demonstrating how the thickness and conductivity of the tissue membrane affects the current profiles near a simple biological tissue model exposed either to ELF uniform current or to ELF nonuniform current.

articleTitle: A new method to determine the 3-D field and transposition way of large generator
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: In the design of a large generator, in order to determine the best transposition way of stator windings so as to avoid circulating and local overheating, it is necessary to accurately calculate the electromagnetic field in the end-windings. Because the shape of the end-windings is complicated, the distributed end-windings are always replaced by continuous equivalent sheet or line current concentrated on the center line of windings, it is unable to calculate the electromagnetic field in the strands of end-windings. In the paper, the end-windings are considered as many rectangular current element rigid bodies, the position-posture matrix in robot mechanics is applied for the first time to describe the current body's position, and 3-D distributed stator current in end-windings is considered exactly. The electromagnetic field in the end winding's strand of a large hydraulic-generator is calculated by an integral method, and then the best transposition way is determined.

articleTitle: Frequency dependence of energy deposition in the multilayered spherical model of a human head near a half wavelength dipole
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: The biological effects on the human body of electromagnetic waves of cellular phones have become a major concern. This paper discusses the evaluation of energy deposition when the human head is approximated by the multilayered concentric spherical model and the cellular phone is by a half wavelength dipole. In this paper, the whole power absorption rate and peak value of specific absorption rate (SAR) in the frequency from 0.1 GHz to 3 GHz is calculated. Moreover, the distance dependence of power absorption rate and peak SAR is obtained.

articleTitle: 1/f phase and correlation noises in transmission media and a frequency noise reduction method in an oscillator
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: Phase and amplitude fluctuations are analyzed in a one-dimensional transmission line and diffusion process of the minority carriers in the base of a bipolar transistor. Both noise measurements were also carried out in a bipolar transistor and a possible method is discussed to decrease the noise. The frequency and current fluctuations and their correlation were also measured in a phase shift transistor oscillator. The spectra are of 1/f type and both are correlated. A demonstration was carried out to reduce the frequency fluctuation and a useful method to reduce the fluctuation is proposed in an oscillator.

articleTitle: The influence of extruded-finned heatsink on noise susceptibility of IC; the case of capacitive coupling
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: This study describes the simulated and experimental results about the influence of an extruded-finned heatsink on the noise susceptibility of an IC. It is concluded that the simulated results by FEM and authors' proposed approximation method to reduce computation time are in good agreement with the experimental results within 2 dB, and the noise susceptibility of the IC increases (immunity degrades) by equipping a heatsink, except susceptibility is down in the resonant frequency of the circuits.

articleTitle: EM compatibility issues in wireless communications
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: The wireless communication band of devices of most commonly used by the public extends from about 27 MHz to 2.2 GHz. Recent advances in the technology of "intelligent" magnetic card reading from a distance of several feet have extended the frequency of wireless personal communications down to 0.12 MHz. The traditional wireless portable communication modulation technology has been frequency modulation (FM); few products used single side band (SSB), which entails linear amplification of the carrier. The explosive demand of channels for cellular telephony has caused the application of more sophisticated modulation technologies (pulsed and linear amplitude modulation). The subscriber units of the newer cell phone technologies produce EM fields in the appropriate RF communication band and low frequency magnetic fields in the modulation baseband (11-217 MHz). These low frequency magnetic fields can interfere with proper functions of other electronic equipment in their immediate vicinity. From the above considerations, it is clear that the EM compatibility challenges in wireless communication technologies extend from few Hz to several GHz. In all frequencies, the EMC challenge arises from the need of evaluating the E and H-fields in the immediate vicinity of their sources and must be averaged either over a small volume to detect the source of disturbance fields which have a sphere of influence with an extremely small radius (e.g. 10-12 cm) with respect to the wavelength of the low frequency (<300 Hz) signal.

articleTitle: Effect of noise suppression by surge protective devices for impulsive noise
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: The response characteristics of surge protective devices for impulsive noise characterized by fast rise times are examined. These response characteristics are calculated in the time domain using an equivalent circuit model for a voltage clamping device. Calculated values were found to agree well with measured values and the appropriateness of the equivalent circuit model was demonstrated. Based on this model, the amount of inductance in low-capacitance devices was found to be a major factor in generating overshoot above the clamp voltage in the noise rising interval.

articleTitle: The BCH coded digital radio communication system under man-made noise environments
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: Man-made radio frequency noise emitted from electrical and electronic apparatus is well known to be a major cause of performance degradation of digital radio communication systems. In this paper, in order to decrease the effect of man-made radio noise on the bit error rate performance of the /spl pi//4-shift QPSK modulation system, we employ the Bose-Chaudhuri-Hocquenghem (BCH) forward error correction coding scheme. Numerical results demonstrate that, under man-made radio noise environments, the improvements in the performances of the /spl pi//4-shift QPSK system can be achieved by using the BCH coding scheme.

articleTitle: Application of ferrite chip EMI suppressors to EMS
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: This paper describes the application of ferrite chip EMI suppressors to EMS (electromagnetic susceptibility). Based on the test results of a basic logic IC on a printed circuit board (PCB) and actual electronic equipment, we recognizes that ferrite chip EMI suppressors have a characteristics of EMS countermeasure components.

articleTitle: Research activities in Japan on biological effects of electromagnetic fields emitted by cellular phones
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: Recent research efforts into the safety problems of cellular phones carried out in Japan are reviewed. The results of the medium-term liver bioassay of rats exposed to 900 MHz and 1.5 GHz TDMA waveforms are summarized with a discussion on the findings. Some other ongoing studies promoted by the committee organized by the Japanese Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications are also briefly reviewed.

articleTitle: Radiated emission from a power plane of a multilayer printed circuit board
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: This paper describes radiated emission from a power plane of multilayer printed circuit boards (PCBs). A multilayer PCB has power planes, ground planes and signal planes. Emission from a power plane contributes to measurement results of emission from PCB. Measurements are made of emissions from multilayer PCBs, which have various lengths power plane areas. The authors examined the influence of the power plane only on radiated emissions.

articleTitle: Measurement and calculation in the near field of dipole antenna using optical electric-field sensor
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: The pulse response of a dipole antenna was measured. Almost the same waveform as the input pulse was detected by an optical electric field sensor, but damped oscillation waveform was measured when a dipole antenna was used as receiving antenna. To investigate this difference, frequency characteristics of a dipole antenna was measured and calculated by the method of moment. As the result, it was clarified that radiation field characteristics of a dipole antenna with tuning frequency of 90 MHz is very wide band and has even frequency component above 1 GHz. On the other hand, reception characteristics of the dipole antenna were calculated and found to be narrow band. This is considered to be cause of the difference for pulse response above mentioned.

articleTitle: Dosimetric analysis of a small animal locally exposed to near fields by electrically short antennas
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: An in vivo experiment of small animals, whose emphasis is put on testing possible promoting effects of 1.5 GHz digital cellular portable telephones on skin carcinogenesis, is being planned and advanced in Japan. The purpose of this paper is to obtain an idea for realizing such an exposure system by using an electrically short antenna and to give its dosimetric analysis.

articleTitle: Parameter determination of equivalent circuit for load effect due to ferrite core attachment
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: Ferrite cores are commonly attached to a cable/wire to suppress the electromagnetic noise from digital information equipment. In this paper, an equivalent circuit for the load effect due to a ferrite core installed inside a coaxial cable is considered. A method for determining the equivalent circuit parameters is presented. The validity is confirmed by measurements of the scattering transmission coefficient S/sub 21/ for commercially available ferrite cores with different dimensions.

articleTitle: A proposal of multi-functioned EM-wave absorbers
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: A multi-functioned EM-wave absorbers are investigated. As one of these fundamental concepts, light reflecting, light emitting and EM-wave radiating type absorbers have been proposed. First, the methods of controlling the matching frequency are investigated as a key technology to realize these kinds of EM-absorber. Simple methods for controlling the matching frequency using magnetized ferrite, ferrite combined with other materials, and ferrite with small holes are summarized. In particular, the detailed matching characteristics of ferrite with small holes are investigated theoretically and experimentally. Secondly, as examples of multi-functional absorbers, the matching characteristics of the light reflecting and the light emitting absorbers at frequencies of 2.45 GHz and 5.8 GHz are clarified.

articleTitle: EFT/B immunity test conditions of telecommunication equipment using ISDN basic interfaces
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: Test conditions are significant factors in testing such as the sweep rate in conducted continuous wave immunity testing, or the duration of impress bursts in EFT/B immunity testing. The effects of various impressed waveforms were measured. Determination of waveform generating parameters for basic ISDN telecommunications equipment is discussed. Communication method of basic ISDN telecommunication equipment is investigated as to physical, data link, and network layers. The most suitable waveform for a basic ISDN interface is discussed.

articleTitle: Accurate relations and probability bounds of errors in the systems with multipositional multidimensional quadrature amplitude shift keying
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: One of the trends of increasing information transmission system frequency-energetic efficiency i.e. increasing the exchange relations between noise immunity and transmission speed, is connected with the development and application of multidimensional signals. Signal quadrature amplitude shift keying (QASK) has been widely used. The report discusses the noise immunity of systems with N-dimensional M-positional QASK: QASK-M/N. Formulas for the calculation of a minimal Euclidean distance under a given maximal and medium signal energies are obtained. A formula for symbol error probability is shown under coherent reception in a constant channel with additive white Gaussian noise, supposing that transmitted messages are probabilistic. Relations equivalent to upper and lower boundaries for P/sub e/ are obtained. On the base of the obtained relations we made a numerical analysis of frequency-energetic efficiency and estimated gain with increasing QASK-M/N signal dimensionality.

articleTitle: Compensating method of CRT display jitter caused by an external magnetic field
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: Magnetic shielding is a useful method for a CRT display that has jitter caused by an external magnetic field. This paper presents the effectiveness of compensation coils as a mitigation method which has many advantages in eliminating this jitter.

articleTitle: Immunity testing of computerized equipment to fast electrical transients using adaptive test methods
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: One of the major problems associated with testing computerized equipment for immunity, stems from the fact that their susceptibility to electrical transients is time-variant. This paper develops an improved statistical model for the susceptibility of computerized equipment to electrical transients and illustrates a few affordable methods for estimating the mean and maximum malfunction probability in an operational cycle. Reinforcement learning algorithms are used to estimate the maximum susceptibility efficiently. These algorithms automatically restrict testing to the most susceptible time windows. This allows affordable testing for safety-related equipment and also supports effective redesign.

articleTitle: Development of statistical parameter measuring equipment
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: A statistical parameter of disturbance is effective to estimate BER degradation of a digital link due to the disturbance. For the statistical parameter, an amplitude probability distribution (APD) gives a characteristic of the amplitude domain of the disturbance, and, furthermore, a crossing rate distribution (CRD) and a pulse duration distribution (PDD) give time domain characteristics. It has been reported that BER degradation of a digital link such as PHS or PDC due to disturbances emitted from microwave ovens can be estimated from the APD data of the disturbance. It is also necessary to obtain the CRD and PDD data of disturbance in order to make a digital link which has countermeasures against burst noise by using interleave techniques, etc. In this paper, APD/CRD/PDD measuring equipment is introduced and demonstrated.

articleTitle: Predicting EMC emissions from printed circuit boards using numerical modeling tools
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: Most signals which cause emissions originate on the printed circuit (PC) board. Naturally, some of these signals are required for proper operation of the device, but often these required signals are coupled into areas where they were not intended and cause potential EMC emissions. Typical PC boards contain many traces which are closely packed together. This makes the analysis of potential emissions very complex and difficult. There is a need for automated prediction tools which divide the total PC board emissions problem into individual problems which can be analyzed quickly and accurately. While there is not one modeling tool which can predict emissions from a complete circuit board CAD file, there are many applications for modeling of emissions from PC boards. Each specific cause must be considered separately, and then modeled individually. This is likely to require a number of different modeling tools and techniques. This analysis is likely to require the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD), the method of moments (MoM) and the partial element equivalent circuit (PEEC) modeling techniques, at different times, for different applications.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic noise induced on unshielded part in shielded pair cable
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: This paper describes an inducing mechanism of the electromagnetic noise in shielded pair cables with an unshielded part. The paper also examines the electromagnetic noise characteristics for an unshielded part considering the height above the ground, pair cable unbalance and pair cable terminal impedance, theoretically and experimentally.

articleTitle: Measurement and simulation of magnetic shielding with ferromagnetic material
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: The measurement and the simulation of magnetic shielding with ferromagnetic material are investigated. The underlying configuration is a laboratory model of the shielding of power cables with constructional steel. The hard- and software for the measurement was developed especially for this purpose. The main aspects are an analog amplification with low noise, a high resolution A/D conversion and digital signal processing. The simulation is done using the finite element method together with the complex effective reluctivity material model, which is fast and reliable. The agreement between measurement and simulation is excellent.

articleTitle: Evaluation of 10 m semi-anechoic chamber characteristics
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: A 10 m semi-anechoic chamber constructed at Matsushita Communication Ind. Co., Ltd. in August 1997 was evaluated. It has wider space than conventional 10 m chambers. By securing nonreflecting object area required by CISPR16-1 at a whole EUT setting area on the 6 m diameter turntable, the influence of absorbers lining the walls could be suppressed in the frequency range of 30 MHz to 100 MHz. Therefore, the deviation from theoretical value was within 2 dB and the dispersion of site attenuation value was within 1 dB among five points, which were center point on the turntable and the front, rear, left and right position 3 meters apart from center. From these experimental results, it was verified that this chamber has the almost same characteristics as an open area test site for EMI measurement.

articleTitle: EMI suppression effects of a magnetic composite sheet with an internal conductive layer
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: With continuing development in the field of digital high-frequency devices, the problems of EMI in the quasi-microwave band are becoming increasingly serious. The authors have previously proposed a noise suppressing sheet made of soft magnetic metal flakes, and its efficacy as a countermeasure for high frequency noise has been confirmed. This sheet is already in practical use in cellular-phones and notebook PCs, installed near radiation sources. This paper describes EMI suppression effects achieved with the use of a new EMI suppression sheet with an internal conductive layer, designed for use in interference suppression between printed circuit boards.

articleTitle: Constrained optimization of the homogeneity of the magnetic field evoked by coils in a shielded room
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: The homogeneity of the magnetic field inside a magnetically shielded room is of great importance in some biomagnetic and other applications. In this paper, the authors report on investigations concerning the optimization of the homogeneity of the magnetic field inside a certain observation volume. The magnetic field is generated by four rectangular current loops placed inside a magnetically shielded room. A comparison is made with results published for unshielded coil systems.

articleTitle: Ferrite powders for chip inductor device
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: The interfacial diffusion between ferrite and Ag during co-firing was investigated using the SEM-EDX technique. It was found that the diffusion increases with the sintering temperature. Some impurities promote the interfacial diffusion. We proposed ferrite powders suitable for the chip inductor devices.

articleTitle: A case study on the reflection of absorbing materials using FDTD
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: The absorber used in anechoic and semi-anechoic chambers employed for emissions and immunity testing is examined. The reflectivity of absorber materials is studied using finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) technique. With the powerful computing resource, the method of homogenization is not used to achieve a more accurate result. General reflectivity guidelines are also listed for comparing absorber used for the EMC testing from 30 MHz to 1 GHz.

articleTitle: Interference characteristics between 2.4-GHz-band middle-speed wireless LANs using direct sequence and frequency hopping
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: Middle-speed (1-to-2-Mbit/sec) 2.4-GHz-band wireless LAN systems are widely used throughout the world. As they occupy the same frequency range, electromagnetic interference will occur between them. We investigated the interference characteristics between wireless LAN systems that use direct sequence (DS) and frequency hopping (FH). Experimental results showed that varying the modulation parameters changed the interference characteristics of the throughputs of wireless LAN systems. Calculated throughput characteristics for the interference agreed with experimental results. Calculating of the DS and FH system performance when E/sub b//N/sub 0/=20 dB showed that the D/U ratio required for the FH system was smaller than those required for the DS systems. However, when the D/U ratio was above 8 dB, the throughputs of the DS systems were higher than that of those FH system. These results clarified the interference characteristics, and will be useful in the prediction of communications performance in environments where DS and FH systems are intermixed.

articleTitle: Computation of shielding effectiveness of concentric spherical shields with plane wave illumination
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: As a basic problem for the multilayer shield, the model of the concentric spherical shields being illuminated by a plane wave is investigated and formulated in a computationally suitable form. The incident plane wave and all the fields involved are expressed in terms of spherical vector wave functions, and each spherical shell is expressed by a 2/spl times/2 matrix which relates the inner field coefficients to the outer field coefficients. To evaluate the shielding effectiveness of the cavity as a whole. The RMS-based SE (shielding effectiveness) is proposed and its analytical form is derived. Several numerical examples concerning the cavity resonance suppression are shown.

articleTitle: EMC chambers for radiated EMC testing up to 18 GHz
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: In the future, EMC measurements above 1 GHz will become mandatory. Currently, most newly realised full-compliance EMC chambers are already specified up to 18 GHz. However, whereas existing standards clearly specify the requirements between 26 MHz and 1 GHz, the standards for the higher frequency range are still in draft form. To construct such chambers, broadband EMC absorbers are required that are effective from 26 MHz to over 18 GHz. The absorber design needs to properly combine both low and high frequency concepts. Measurement results up to 18 GHz are shown for state-of-the-art anechoic EMC chambers for 3, 5 and 10 m test distance.

articleTitle: Automatic immunity tester relating to RF-conducted disturbance
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: The authors describe a new design for an automatic immunity tester relating to RF-conducted disturbance, which incorporates coupling-decoupling networks (CDN) and exchange simulators (EXS) into the housing, and is applicable to EUT such as telecommunications equipment.

articleTitle: Thin wave absorbers for quasi-microwave band: effect of polymer permittivity on wave absorption for polymer composites containing magnetic metal particles
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: The effect of polymer permittivity on wave absorption in the quasimicrowave band has been clarified for polymer composites containing magnetic metal particles. It was found that the higher the real part and the lower the imaginary part of the permittivity, the thinner the absorber. However, in polymer or polymer composites, the real increases with an increase in the imaginary part. This means one must carefully choose the polymer species at the crossing area of the real and imaginary parts of the permittivity when designing absorbers.

articleTitle: Thinner electromagnetic wave absorbers using ferroelectric substances
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: Two types of electromagnetic wave absorbers using ferroelectric materials have been studied. Ferroelectric materials are superior to ferromagnetic ones at frequencies in the above gigahertz range, because their permeability does not decrease as much. In one type of absorber, a resistive film was placed in front of the ferroelectric material. In the other, a ferroelectric layer was placed in front of a soft-magnetic layer. Placing a resistive film in front of the ferroelectric material made it possible to design wave absorbers even though the real and imaginary parts of the permittivity did not fulfill the matching condition. Both absorbers could be made thinner than conventional carbonyl iron-loaded rubber ones and still work well at frequencies above giga-hertz. Furthermore, the matching frequency can reduce to the quasi-microwave-band range by placing a ferroelectric layer in front of the carbonyl iron-loaded rubber.

articleTitle: Recent topics in CISPR [EMC standards organisation]
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: This paper presents the recent activities of the International Special Committee of Radio Interference (CISPR) which is one of the standard-making-international organizations in the field of electromagnetic compatibility.

articleTitle: Application of fuzzy logic in EMC constraint PCB design
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: Application of fuzzy logic structures in the EMC constraint PCB design substantially improves quality of design solutions by providing designers with flexibility in layout. Fuzzy logic structures are applied successfully for selection of EMC constraint design solutions in conjunction with the constructive algorithms.

articleTitle: Resonant characteristics of parallel plate waveguide cavities with irises
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: This paper shows the analysis of electromagnetic scattering by parallel plate waveguide cavities. The internal region is separated into two areas by additional plates, which arises internal coupling problems. The applied numerical technique here is the point matching method considering the edge condition. As a numerical example, the radar cross section is presented for the E-polarized case and the H-polarized case. The authors clarify the internal contribution in terms of the cavity resonances.

articleTitle: Beam diffraction by rectangular cylinders
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: The uniform theory of diffraction and the complex source point method are used together to predict two-dimensional scattering by rectangular cylinders by E and H polarized beam sources. Arrays of beams representing antenna patterns are also used to model propagation into the shadow regions of buildings.

articleTitle: On the estimation of ESD current waveshapes by radiated electromagnetic fields
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: This paper presents the method for an estimation of ESD current waveshapes by radiated electromagnetic fields. The method of current waveshape estimation described uses the one-antenna method (single field method) and two-antenna method (complex field method) with a measured electric or magnetic field at a given field point by a time domain antenna. In order to verify the availability of the estimation theory, the ESD current waveform estimation were performed by one and two antenna methods using the measured electric fields of Wilson and Ma (1991) and compared with experiments.

articleTitle: Recent movement in VCCI [Voluntary Laboratory Accreditation Center]
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: The fundamental rules of the Voluntary Control Council for Interference (VCCI) were presented. Recent movement in the VCCI was also presented with some statistics. The Voluntary Laboratory Accreditation Center (VLAC) inaugurated in 1998 was introduced. Thereby, it was shown that how successfully the VCCI had controlled the EMI of information technology equipment (ITE) placed onto the Japanese market.

articleTitle: The ULF electromagnetic radiation excited by special typical minor clumped earthquakes
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: A group of more than 250 typical minor clumped earthquakes occurred from July 25 to August 17 in 1993 in Xianning, Hubei province, central China. Just 40 days before the first minor quake occurred, a series of intriguing electromagnetic radiation anomalies (EMRA) were observed at Wuhan electromagnetic seismic monitoring station (30/spl deg/ 37' 12" N, 114/spl deg/ 21' 52" E). Observations of the empirical phenomena showed that premonitory ULF EMRA hints preceding or during the Xianning typical minor clumped earthquakes could be distinctively spotted among the ubiquitous electromagnetic background by some sensitive receiving device. Further analysis indicated the ULF EMRA duration time had a negative relationship with the time interval from the ULF EMRA appearance to certain earthquake occurrence. The electromagnetic amplitude and wave mode of the ULF EMRA were complicated, sometimes it behaved like irregular moderate vibration appearing by a displaced dynamic zero point, at other times it appeared as an intensive electromagnetic impulse. Finally, the ULF EMRA information preceding or during the Xinning earthquakes was not observed on the right earthquakes' occurrence time.

articleTitle: NEMP coupling to integrated building distribution network
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: Lives now depend much more on the information infrastructure. The Integrated Building Distribution Network (IBDN) is one of the most important parts of the information infrastructure, which should be reliable and flexible. The harmful effects from nuclear electromagnetic pulse (NEMP) are discussed in this paper. The conclusions can be used for general electromagnetic pulse cases.

articleTitle: Evaluation of impedance-matching and coupling by using radiowave holography method. II
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: A new method for evaluating microwave modules is proposed. The technique yields visualization of impedance mismatching points and electromagnetic coupling by using a radiowave holography method based on the near-field interference pattern measurement. Some results of experiments are presented to demonstrate the validity of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Indoor propagation experiments in shielding TV studio at 2 GHz and analysis by geometrical optics method
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: Indoor propagation experiments in a shielding studio were carried out to obtain information on the multipath propagation at 2 GHz. This paper describes indoor propagation property in the shielding TV studio and applicability of the geometrical optics method to the propagation prediction. First, the reflectivity of walls and a floor of the shielding studio are evaluated. The authors analyze the delay profiles and electric field strength distribution in the studio with the geometrical optics method using evaluated reflectivity. The geometrical optics method is found to be practically applicable to predict the multipath propagation inside the shielding studio. The delay spread can be evaluated from calculations approximately within a 10% deviation when multiple reflection up to 12 times is taken into account. This calculation method can also predict the overall trend of the electric field strength distribution in the shielding studio.

articleTitle: Reconsideration of CISPR24 immunity test condition and performance criteria of TTE
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: This paper describes a problem relating to the requirements for an RF continuously conducted immunity test specified in CISPR Publication 24 (CISPR24), and proposes a modification on the basis of experimental considerations. From the proposals now being discussed within CISPR Sub-Committee G (CISPR/SCG), the state of discussions taking account of comments from national committees is also outlined.

articleTitle: Open-circuit voltages due to lightning-generated time-dependent and elliptically polarized E-fields
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: The open-circuit voltage induced by an incident EM field generated by lightning may cause damage in electronic devices. An ideal and less realistic time-independent and linearly polarized E-field has been often used to predict this important parameter. This study generalizes the E-field incident to be time-dependent and elliptically polarized, and calculates the open-circuit voltages under this new environment for two popular but simple cable configurations. These results are then compared to those generated under the ideal and less realistic environment.

articleTitle: An example of modern radio disturbance measuring apparatus and systems
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: The disturbance strength measuring instrument (KNM-S243/S603) is the newest type of measuring instrument that automatically measures electromagnetic interference conformance with CISPR, VDE, FCC, MIL, EN, VCCI and other national standards. A 16-bit CPU is built in and measurements are quickly carried out according to each national standard and the measured data is output on a CRT, printer and plotter. A turntable, antenna mast, LISN, clamp carrier etc. can be controlled and a radiation noise, transmission noise or other general measurement system can be built by dedicated application software. The measured data can also be output to printer and plotter in an output format conforming to each national standard.

articleTitle: Effect of regenerative amplification of atmospherics in field ELF registering complexes
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: The effect of regenerative amplification of atmospherics in the field ELF registering complexes is considered. It is shown that this effect is observed in the frequency range 200-900 Hz in the conditions of using of certain aerials and grounding with the presence of increased damping of the ELF waves, for example in day time. Some practical consequences are discussed.

articleTitle: Far-end crosstalk waveform for CMOS-IC and diode loads
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: Crosstalk noise, which leads malfunction in data transmission equipment, is one of the most important problems to be solved. In this study, a CMOS-IC, a silicon diode, and a variable capacitance diode are used as nonlinear loads of microstrip lines. The waveform of the far-end crosstalk is measured and analyzed using a 4-port network model in the time domain. It is shown that the C-V characteristics of the diodes influence the waveform of the crosstalk, and that it is valid to calculate the waveform considering the capacitance of the loads to be fixed if the dependence of the capacitance upon the voltage is small.

articleTitle: Lightning surge protectors for LAN equipment
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: Lightning protectors for 10 Base-5, 10 Base-T, and 100 Base-T LAN equipment have been developed, providing high-quality and inexpensive surge protection with avalanche diodes, variable resistors, and gas tube arrestors. Tap connectors are used with coaxial cables and shielded modular connectors with twisted pair cables, reducing the time and effort needed to attach the protectors.

articleTitle: Some multi-dimensional generalization in space and time domains for Middleton's study in stochastic evaluation of correlative many EM noise processes
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: In this paper, a statistical electromagnetic (abbr., EM) interference study is constructed mainly from a theoretical viewpoint on the basis of an N-dimensional random walk problem in the multi-dimensional signal space. The effectiveness of the proposed method is experimentally confirmed through an acoustic type simulation experiment with joint space-time nonPoisson interference as one of the same wave motion type environments as the EM environment, and an application to an actual EM environment.

articleTitle: Rating EMC parameters of microelectronic systems maintaining safety in response to actual electromagnetic environment
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: The report deals with the development of a new method of rating EMC parameters of microelectronic safety systems using the probability approach as recommended by the IEC 610000-401 Guides. EMC parameters are rated using the probabilistic criteria of EMC levels assumed as a numerical value of failure probability. For user's convenience an EMCpar package in the Windows environment has been devised allowing to determine noise and noise immunity levels to be rated at specified EMC standards. The new method is better tailored to the task because it allows to determine EMC parameters to be rated according to the specified standards of reliable and safe performance of microelectronic systems.

articleTitle: Influence of the high voltage overhead cable on the bearing station with short wave and its testing of the shield distance and calculation
publicationTitle: 1999 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (IEEE Cat. No.99EX147)
abstract: The influence of high-voltage overhead cables on the radio bearing station with short wave comes from two aspects: one is the source, i.e. the radio interference of the high-voltage overhead cable; the other is the nonsource, i.e. the secondary radiation of the various conductors of the high-voltage overhead cable. The radio interference of the high-voltage overhead cable mainly comes from the cable corona and spark discharges. Compared with the environment noise, the corona and spark discharge, due to its existence, cause the lower noise degree rise higher, the pulse density increases. This radio interference has a certain direction, but the bearing is wide, so its influence corresponds to a raised background noise level and reduced receiving sensitivity of the short wave radio bearing station. At the same time, it has a certain deviation influence on the direction indication (azimuth) of the short wave single channel radio direction finder (especially when the direction of the incoming wave and high-voltage overhead cable are close to parallel), but this radio influence, thanks to its wide bearing, is not obvious. The influence of various conductors of the high-voltage overhead cable line and its parts, especially the perpendicular grounding posts, their secondary radiation influence is rather obvious, thus the author calculates and demonstrates the influence.
